scope: Continuous phone geolocation repair; not acceptance of the full original map-software plan.
codeFindings: A provider counter was incorrectly assigned performance.timeOrigin and could be rejected after page uptime increased.
The original recovery timer was cleared by the first accepted fix and never rearmed for a subsequent stalled watch.

clockCompatibility.policy: OpenHarmony/ArkWeb callbacks use receipt time; other browsers retain Unix timestamp validation.
clockCompatibility.notes: The actual provider timestamp format was not measured. Clock regression inputs were synthetic, based on the reported failure and working reference implementation.

recovery.errors: Alternate accuracy modes; back off persistent errors up to 30 s; stop automatic retries on permission denial.
recovery.lifecycle: Retire old watch/request callbacks on retry, permission denial, backgrounding and page-cache restoration.

validation.browserScope: Chrome with injected geolocation and orientation; recovery cases use a virtual clock installed before navigation. Integration covers real map routes, publishing, offline reload and an actual navigate API request with an ArkWeb-like counter.
validation.integrationReleaseNote: The 12 integration tests used the existing online routing/terrain schema (v5/v3) plus the new frontend, before the final error-backoff-only adjustment. The final 11 recovery tests include that adjustment. The user then deployed the whole current workspace (v6/v4); the staged v5/v3 package was not deployed.

deviceValidation.requestedScenario: Reopen in OpenHarmony WeChat, observe about one minute while moving, then background and return.

remainingScope: Independent registration/passability benchmarks and broader original-plan acceptance remain tracked in IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md. The reported continuous-location incident is confirmed resolved by the user.
